audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict '10 100 1010' (initial primary, penult secondary from 4 syllables, trisyllables no secondary) matches Douglas 1968=1976 exactly, and the learner's guide and WALS (Initial/Fixed) agree on the primary; StressTyp2 is silent; no source read says anything different. The deciding work is a 1968 AIAS grammar sketch, but Glottolog (86 refs, zero phonology items) and Crossref/IA searches show no phonology article, instrumental study or fuller grammar exists, so it is probably the best available; hence 'adequate' rather than 'thin'. Not 'well-sourced' because (a) the catalog record's quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty — the Douglas quotation lives only in the owner note — and (b) Douglas is held as full-text snippets from the two archive.org scans, not as a page image. sources.quote: 'In Noongar the stress is always on the first syllable, which is unlike English where in many words the stress is on the second syllable.' Examples yong/ka, dje/na, ka/ri, bi/di/ba/ba, dji/ba-djo/ba/liny with first syllable (and each compound member's first syllable) bold.

sources.quote: Initial primary; trisyllables decreasing stress; other polysyllables secondary on penult; compounds member-initial primary+secondary; reduplications equal stress on each stem-initial; 'predictable and non-phonemic'. Both editions agree verbatim; the owner note's one bridged junction is closed verbatim by the held snippet.
